header: 3HumanVerse: Scaling Egocentric Whole-Body Data Collection in the Open World

images.caption: Figure 2:HumanVerse.The wearable capture setup, task and motion distributions, and paired egocentric video and whole-body motions illustrate the dataset’s scale and diversity.

Figure 3:Robot-free capture, curation, and robot alignment.We select open-world scenes and tasks and record egocentric video, body motion, and speech with a robot-matched camera viewpoint. Curation includes synchronization, language/task annotation, body and hand motion reconstruction, observation alignment, action alignment, and quality inspection. Modality thumbnails are schematic.
Figure 4:Representative examples fromHumanVerse.Sixty first-person frames are arranged in a12×512\times 5gallery to illustrate diversity in tasks, scenes, objects, and hand–object interactions.

Figure 5:Synchronized human motion and egocentric observations.Top: egocentric RGB frames. Bottom: corresponding SMPL body meshes with MANO hand motion and illustrative camera frusta.
Camera frusta schematically illustrate viewing direction.

Figure 6:Human-to-humanoid action alignment.The first two stages modify the human and robot references. The third accounts for execution dynamics and directly optimizes motion tokens using gradient-based updates. End-effector targets remain fixed throughout. Rendered poses illustrate the procedure and are not experimental rollouts.
